clue.text: Boot alumni out, as questionably placed

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some school has expelled its former pupils, on doubtful grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals an anagram of BOOT and ALUMNI; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being far out along a branch is an idiom for being in an exposed, precarious position.

clue.text: Violent attack along roadway — hoot en route

parts.note: on can mean along or onward, as in 'move on'

indicators.note: en route means on the way, so the laugh sits within the street

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a hoot is a loud laugh

explanation.surface: Someone hooting while driving along a road is a violent attack on the ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoot' suggests a car horn on the road, but here it is a burst of laughter carried 'en route'.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, violent assault, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Object to water, over a gallon

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, that is above, the next

parts.note: to water down a drink is to dilute or thin it

explanation.surface: Someone protests at watering something with more than a gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb (to protest) but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any object or item, a plain synonym.

clue.text: State briefly part of answer

parts.note: the short form of this Australian state's name, three letters, appears within the word 'answer' (aNSWer)

explanation.surface: An instruction to summarise part of a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation NSW is found inside the clue word 'answer'; expand it to the full state name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a state of south-eastern Australia, whose capital is Sydney, abbreviated NSW.

clue.text: Still inside overdue baby needs this

indicators.note: inside places one word within the other

parts.note: overdue means late
still in the sense 'even now' means yet

explanation.surface: Even now, a baby that is past its due date needs something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as calm or motionless, but here it means 'even now'; 'inside' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the set of clothes and bedding prepared for a newborn baby.

clue.text: Endless structure erected enclosing northern state

indicators.note: enclosing means the reversed word wraps around the next piece
erected means set upright, which in a down clue turns the letters to read upwards
endless means the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: anatomy is bodily structure

explanation.surface: An unfinished building is put up around a state in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: ANATOMY loses its last letter ('Endless') to give ANATOM; 'erected' reverses it to MOTANA, 'enclosing' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Montana is one of the United States, in the north-west bordering Canada.

clue.text: Narrow strip of land needs a little light rain

definitions.meaning: a long narrow point of land jutting into the sea
to sprinkle a few drops, as in 'it's beginning to rain lightly'

explanation.definitionFit: Spit names both a sandy spit projecting into water and a few drops of drizzle.

clue.text: Got a foretaste before rival married

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before
to rival is to vie with
wed means married

explanation.surface: Someone saw a hint of what was coming before a rival married.
explanation.definitionFit: To have previewed something is to have seen or sampled it in advance.

clue.text: Subject to having enough members, elect leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A rule says a vote can happen only if a quorum of members is present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first letter of each of 'to having enough members elect'.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Launching place has rock round rim

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to rock is to sway
a lip is a rim or edge

explanation.surface: A place where something is launched has a rocky edge around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' is a verb, SWAY, not a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipway is a sloping ramp from which boats are launched into the water.

clue.text: Two presents in limbo

parts.note: present in time is now; present in place is here
present in time is now; present in place is here

explanation.surface: Two gifts are stuck in limbo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' looks like gifts but means two senses of 'present': in time and in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in limbo is in an indeterminate state, going nowhere, in no place at all.

clue.text: New bit appears faulty — ditch it in here

indicators.note: faulty suggests something broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new part seems defective, so throw it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' signals an anagram of NEW BIT APPEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastepaper bin is the receptacle into which rubbish is ditched.

clue.text: Silver and gold taken back after end of prize-giving, causing belligerence

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
taken back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Medals are reclaimed after a ceremony, causing a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' reverses OR to RO; G is the last letter of 'prize-giving'. AGGRO is British slang for aggressive trouble-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal British slang for aggressive, hostile behaviour.

clue.text: Unusual terrapins come to light

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange turtles emerge into view.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpire is to become known, as when a fact emerges or is revealed.

clue.text: Let cat out of bag — dispose of bag for nothing

definitions.meaning: to hand over a hunter's bag of shot birds free of charge

explanation.walkthrough: A hunter's 'bag' is the game shot; giving it away is disposing of it for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to betray a secret, the same as letting the cat out of the bag.

clue.text: Greenish-blue coat on copper; composer has grey in France

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer
gris is French for grey

explanation.surface: A composer is given a grey look while in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdigris is the green-blue patina that forms on copper and brass when exposed to air.

clue.text: I seek many changes in American behaviour

indicators.note: many changes means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone looks for numerous alterations in American conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' signals an anagram of I SEEK MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yankeeism is a characteristically American trait, habit or expression.

clue.text: Ninth horse down -— a shambles - — concede defeat

indicators.note: a shambles is a disorderly mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The ninth horse has fallen, and the race is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shambles' signals an anagram of NINTH HORSE DOWN A.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw in one's hand is a card-playing idiom for giving up or admitting defeat.

clue.text: Short story — star restricts length

indicators.note: restricts means confines, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A celebrity limits the length of a brief tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests a celebrity, but it is NOVA, which holds ELL, an old unit of cloth length.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a work of fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a novel.

clue.text: It's better to drink noisily, after dropping litre on a ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it
after dropping means the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: It is better to slurp a drink, once a litre has spilt aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after dropping' removes the litre; in a down clue 'on' stacks the first piece above the rest. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass is to exceed or do better than, a verb synonym.

clue.text: What's offered to kiss rebuffed by sweetheart, hence unexpected censequence

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: lips are what one offers for a kiss
a lover is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A rejected kiss from a sweetheart leads to unforeseen results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' turns LIPS into SPIL; 'by' and 'hence' are links. 'censequence' is a scanning slip for 'consequence'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spillover is a knock-on effect, an unintended result spreading beyond its source.

clue.text: Exceptionally good policeman

definitions.meaning: short for superintendent, a senior police rank

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for excellent and also short for a police superintendent.

clue.text: Standard? This is better than that

definitions.meaning: a Roman legion's ... was its standard
in golf this score is two under par, the standard score, so better than it

explanation.walkthrough: 'that' points back to 'Standard': par is golf's standard score.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird was the Roman military standard, and in golf the term means two strokes under par.

clue.text: Band surrounded husband

parts.note: girt is an old past tense of gird, meaning encircled

explanation.surface: A ring encircled a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A girth is a band fastened round a horse's belly to hold the saddle.

clue.text: Troops look around for cover

parts.note: paras are paratroopers

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Soldiers search about for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the reversal of the old interjection; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a sunshade, a cover against the sun.

clue.text: German king, composer, architect and writer

definitions.meaning: Domenico ..., Italian composer remembered for the ... bass
Leon Battista ..., Renaissance architect and author

explanation.definitionFit: The name fits a medieval German ruler, an Italian composer and a Renaissance architect-writer.

clue.text: Spots spate

definitions.meaning: an outbreak of red spots on the skin
a sudden run of events, as in a series of burglaries

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an eruption on the skin and a sudden outbreak of incidents.

clue.text: Statesman dancing with them, so they say

indicators.note: so they say means the words are heard spoken

parts.note: dancing with them is waltzing 'em

explanation.surface: A politician dances with them, or so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'waltzing 'em' resembles the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Walsingham was Elizabeth I's principal secretary and spymaster, a Tudor statesman.
